thread:
Elaine: kicking off canary for nimbus19b (int4) on dedicated pool — 5% traffic so far. seeing OOMs when requests with long generations (~800-1200 tokens) hit. unclear if fragmentation or kv-prefetch blowup. anyone familiar with recent int4 behaviour?
Sam: saw similar on another model last month. quick mitigation is to lower max_new_tokens default for the route. canary should use 512 not 1024.
Mike: also check batching window. if small requests get grouped with a large max_new, KV cache grows. try "batch_max_tokens" cap.
Elaine: good point. current route has `max_new_tokens: 1024`, `batch_max_tokens: 4096`, `prefetch_kv: true`. guess that's optimistic.
infra-bot: metric alert — nimbus19b-canary: oom_rate=0.048, avg_latency_tokens=1.2ms, kv_memory_p90=72%
Viv: int4 quant sometimes increases fragmentation for long KV sequences. fallback to int8 for sequences > 512 is a pragmatic short-term fix. we can expose model-variant routing.
Joao: another operational quickie — set `prefetch_kv=false` for the canary traffic slice. also set `kv_eviction_threshold: 0.8` to force earlier trim.
Sam: here's a minimal route patch we used elsewhere:
```
route: /nimbus19b/canary
settings:
  max_new_tokens: 512
  batch_max_tokens: 2048
  prefetch_kv: false
  kv_eviction_threshold: 0.8
  fallback_model: nimbus19b-int8
```
apply as a canary to 5% first.
Elaine: applying now to canary slice. will monitor OOM and token latency. thanks.
Mike: follow-up: if OOMs persist, toggle `adaptive_window: false` to avoid coalescing windows with long tails. that reduced p99 on a different model.
Viv: and add a targeted eval run: generation-quality vs baseline on 100 prompt set at max_new=512 & 1024 to ensure fallback doesn't degrade answers. Sam, can you schedule?
Sam: yeah I'll queue a quick eval job and add it to the rollout checklist. also tagging @eng-sre for tracing if OOMs spike after config flip.
Elaine: update — canary config rolled at 17:08 UTC. baseline oom_rate dropped to 0.01 after 15 min. leaving canary running for 2h then bump to 20% if stable. :thumbsup:
Joao: noted. I'll prepare a follow-up notebook to profile KV growth per step for int4 vs int8 and share results.
Elaine: perfect. thanks all.
notes: canary -> reduce defaults, prefetch off, fall back to int8 for long sequences, add evals
